title: Algebraic Relaxation of Strong-to-Weak Symmetry-Breaking Order via Charge-Sector Broadening
abstract: Strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) is a distinctive phenomenon of mixed quantum states, characterized by nonlinear long-range order associated with strong symmetry. In realistic open quantum systems, however, strong symmetry is macroscopically fragile and can be explicitly reduced to weak symmetry through local charge exchange with the environment. In this paper, we investigate how the SW-SSB order decays under such strong-symmetry-breaking Liouvillian dynamics. For discrete $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry, a local symmetry-breaking perturbation drives an exponential decay of the Rényi-1 long-range correlator, revealing the fragility of discrete SW-SSB order. By contrast, for continuous $U(1)$ symmetry, local charge exchange broadens the distribution over symmetry-charge sectors and leads to parametrically slower algebraic relaxation. We establish a rigorous algebraic lower bound on the connected Rényi-1 long-range correlation, demonstrating the robustness of this slow relaxation. In the thermodynamic limit, we further uncover a two-stage dynamical scaling: $\tilde{R}_1\sim t^{-1}$ at early times and $\tilde{R}_1\sim t^{-1/z}$ at long times, with $z$ set by the underlying hydrodynamic dynamics. As a numerical verification, we consider fermionic chains with $z=2$ and $z=4$, which are excellent agreement with the theoretical predictions.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the decay of order associated with Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking (SW-SSB) in open quantum systems. It distinguishes between discrete ($Z_2$) and continuous ($U(1)$) symmetries, finding that discrete order decays exponentially while continuous order relaxes algebraically. The methodology involves using connected Rényi correlators and analyzing charge-sector dynamics to derive universal scaling laws.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the long-range order associated with Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking (SW-SSB) decays when the strong symmetry is explicitly broken by coupling to an environment.
main_result: The decay rate depends on the symmetry: discrete $Z_2$ symmetry shows exponential decay, while continuous $U(1)$ symmetry exhibits a parametrically slower algebraic relaxation with a universal two-stage scaling law.
method: The analysis uses the connected Rényi-$k$ correlator ($	ilde{R}_k$) and compares the full mixed state to an auxiliary state derived from charge-sector weights to establish rigorous lower bounds on the decay.
model_or_system: The study considers open quantum systems governed by Liouvillian dynamics, specifically examining fermionic chains with local charge exchange coupling to a reservoir. Symmetries analyzed include discrete $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and continuous $U(1)$.
key_observables: Connected Rényi-1 correlator ($	ilde{R}_1$), connected Rényi-2 correlator ($	ilde{R}_2$), and the charge variance ($\sigma_Q^2$).
important_parameters: The hydrodynamic exponent $z$, the coupling strength $\kappa$, and the time evolution $t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing lower bounds by comparing the true correlator to an auxiliary state, often assuming Gaussian distributions for charge fluctuations in the thermodynamic limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the exponential decay for $Z_2$ symmetry and the algebraic relaxation for $U(1)$ symmetry, showing the two-stage scaling $	ilde{R}_1 \sim t^{-1}$ followed by $	ilde{R}_1 \sim t^{-1/z}$.
paper_structure: The paper first analyzes the $Z_2$ case showing exponential decay. It then focuses on the $U(1)$ case, deriving lower bounds for $	ilde{R}_k$ by analyzing the charge-sector dynamics, leading to the identification of the two-stage algebraic scaling law.
why_interesting: This work provides deep insights into how information-theoretic order (like SSB) persists or decays in realistic, dissipative quantum environments, which is crucial for understanding quantum coherence and thermalization.
